input: Map all the hiking trails within two hours away

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The starting point determines the entire geographic search area — without it, no trails can be identified.
Two hours could mean driving, public transit, or walking, which dramatically changes the radius covered.
Trail difficulty, length, or elevation filters determine which trails are actually relevant vs. noise.
Whether this is for solo use, a group, or people with specific physical needs changes which trails qualify.
The output format — a printed map, a saved list in an app, a shared link — shapes the entire workflow.
Trail character preferences (scenic views, waterfalls, forests, dog-friendly, etc.) narrow down what to highlight on the map.
Knowing whether the goal is a quick personal reference or a thorough shareable resource sets the depth of research needed.

gold.taskTitle: Map hiking trails within two hours away
gold.taskDescription: Find and map all hiking trails reachable within a two-hour travel radius from the user's location.

questions.title: What city or address are you starting from?
questions.description: Identify the user's starting location to define the geographic search area for the two-hour radius.

questions.title: Does two hours mean driving, transit, or walking?
questions.description: Determine the mode of travel used to calculate the two-hour boundary.

questions.title: Are there difficulty or length limits for the trails?
questions.description: Establish any filters such as easy/moderate/hard, minimum or maximum trail length, or elevation gain thresholds.

questions.title: Who will be hiking — solo, family, or a group?
questions.description: Understand the hiking party composition to account for accessibility, pace, or group-specific trail requirements.

questions.title: What tool should the final map be built in?
questions.description: Determine whether the output should be in Google Maps, AllTrails, a printed map, a spreadsheet, or another format.

questions.title: What kind of scenery or trail features matter most to you?
questions.description: Capture preferences such as waterfalls, viewpoints, forests, dog-friendly paths, or loop vs. out-and-back trails.

questions.title: Is this a quick personal list or a thorough shareable resource?
questions.description: Clarify the intended depth and audience of the final map to set the right level of research and detail.
